question.problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis in the direction of increasing $x.$ When the displacement of $P$ from the origin $O$ is $x$ meters, the velocity is given by $v(x)=(1+x)\,m/s.$ Initially, $P$ is at the origin $O.$ Find $x$ as a function of time $t.$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14139845/assets/a8a6f49ead700bee856b1bbdbb10848eac0a57609da14e3967916a36eb56f048.png)

We're given that the velocity function $v(x)$ is

$$
v(x)=1+x.
$$

We know that $v=\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.$ Therefore, we have the equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=1+x.
$$

Separating the variables and integrating both sides with respect to $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =1+x \\ \frac{1}{1+x}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =1 \\ \int \frac{1}{1+x}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t & =\int \,\text{d}t \\ \int \frac{1}{1+x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \,\text{d}t \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡|1+x| & =t+K \\ 1+x & =C{e}^{t} \\ x & =C{e}^{t}-1\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $x=0$ when $t=0.$ Therefore, $C=1,$ and the particular solution is

$$
x(t)={e}^{t}-1.
$$
